messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

**Sidecar**
*Chat built for the person catching up, not the person typing.*

Most team chat is designed around the live conversation. That's fine until you manage eight engineers across three time zones and someone has to read 400 messages before standup. Sidecar is built for that reader.

**Channels expire.** Every channel gets an owner and an end date. When a project ships, the channel archives itself and the decisions inside it get pinned to a searchable record. No more 60 dead channels nobody will admit to creating.

**Threads are the default, not the escape hatch.** Replies open in a thread automatically. Main channel view stays a timeline of decisions — one line each, scannable in under a minute.

**Incident mode.** Type `/incident`, and Sidecar spins up a room, pages the on-call rotation from PagerDuty or Opsgenie, timestamps every message, and hands you a timeline you can paste straight into a postmortem. No note-taker required.

**What it doesn't do.** No video calls. No stories, no reactions leaderboard, no AI summarizing your team back to you. We integrate with Zoom and Meet and stop there.

**For the person signing the invoice.** SAML SSO and SCIM on every paid plan, not just enterprise. Audit log export, per-channel retention rules, EU data residency. Self-hosted option if your compliance team asks.

Import from Slack keeps your history, threads, and channel structure intact. Most teams finish the migration over a weekend.

Free for 30 days, no card. $6 per seat after that.
